description:
Found by s507d checking what -E enables.  perl 5.40.3 vs pcl on main 50dbd195:
  printf "use feature ':5.40';\ntry { die \"x\\\\n\" } catch (\$e) { print \"caught \$e\" }\n" > t2.pl
  perl t2.pl -> caught x
  pcl  t2.pl -> PCL: statement dropped at t2.pl line 2: try ... -- Bug. Fell through. Missing case ...
                then dies "PCL: statement not supported at t2.pl line 2"
The same with `pcl -E 'try {...} catch ($e) {...}'`, because -E IS `use feature ':5.40'; use builtin ':5.40';` in front of the program (PCLSwitches::_prefix).
Works: `use v5.40;` before the try, `use feature 'try';`, and `pcl -E 'use feature "try"; try ...'` on one line.
Likely the PPI feature-include callback (the #360 family) recognises the bundle of `use v5.NN` but not the `:5.NN` bundle names of `use feature`.  The fix belongs to that callback in Pl/, not to -E.  docs/pcl-commands.md notes the workaround under -E until it is fixed.
subject: `try`/`catch` is not recognised under `use feature ':5.40'` (a feature BUNDLE), so `pcl -E 'try { die "x\n" } catch ($e) { print "caught $e" }'` drops the statement and dies "statement not supported" (perl: caught x); `use v5.40` and `use feature 'try'` work (found by s507d, main 50dbd195)
